# Legacy DataSet: table families

> Generated by `tools/` from the inputs in `source/`. Every statement below is backed by assembly metadata, IL, or a supplied export sample.
> Anything that could not be proven from those inputs is marked **Unknown** rather than guessed.

**Confidence: CrossVerified.** The container was read byte-for-byte from both
supplied samples, and `Barsa.Meta.DataExchange.SerializationHelper2` names the
same pipeline in metadata.

## Container

```
<file>.metaexport
  └── GZip                                     (magic 1F 8B, "max speed")
        └── .NET BinaryFormatter graph         (header 00 01 00 00 00 FF FF FF FF)
              └── System.Data.DataSet
                    ├── "DataSet.RemotingVersion"  → System.Version
                    ├── "XmlSchema"                → XSD, one xs:element per table
                    └── "XmlDiffGram"              → diffgr:diffgram, one node per row
```

Corroborating metadata:

- `SerializationHelper2.BinarySerializeToFile(string, System.Data.DataSet)`
- `SerializationHelper2.DeserializeDataSetFromFile(string) : System.Data.DataSet`
- the compression argument type `Barsa.Spl.SerializationUtil+CompressionType`

The declared XML encoding inside the package is `utf-16`, but the bytes are
UTF-8, because `BinaryFormatter` writes strings as UTF-8. A reader must ignore
the declaration. This pack's reader does.

> **Security note.** `BinaryFormatter` deserialization of an untrusted package is
> a remote-code-execution risk. This extractor never deserializes; it reads the
> two embedded XML strings out of the byte stream directly.

## Not a ZIP

The spec anticipated `.zip` packages. The supplied samples are not ZIPs. The
export file dialog in `ApplicationExportForm.btnSelectFile_Click` does carry
both a `.metaexport` and a `.zip` filter, so a ZIP variant may exist — but no
sample demonstrates it, so its structure is **Unknown**.

## Table families

| Family | Prefix | Meaning | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Export control | `$` | Session bookkeeping and importer instructions, not payload. | Verified |
| Metadata core | `MET_` / `met_` | The metamodel: systems, types, fields, relations, reports, folders, code. | CrossVerified |
| Version tracking | `Ver_` | Meta-system version records. | Verified |
| Security | `Spl_` / `sec_` | Trustee access and security settings. | Verified |
| Shared objects | `Shr_` | File attachments. | Verified |
| Dynamic entity data | `dyn_<n>` | Rows of user-defined entities; columns are positional `F1..Fn`. | CrossVerified |
| Model-scoped data | `m01_` / `m02_` | Rows of named entities belonging to a model. | Verified |
| Logging / app | `ulog_` / `xapp_` | Use-case logging and app service tables. | Verified |

The `dyn_*` and `m0*_` names are not fixed: the package carries
`$Data_TypeDefDbNames` and `$Data_FieldDefDbNames`, which map type and field ids
to their physical table and column names. A reader that hard-codes `dyn_122_1`
will break on the next system. Resolve through those two tables instead.

## Control tables

| Table | Columns | Role | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$Header` | 7 | Provenance: source database, core version, export time, page count. | Verified |
| `$RootSelection` | 11 | The nodes the operator picked in the export tree. | Verified |
| `$Selection` | 11 | The full closure actually exported, after reference expansion. | Verified |
| `$DeletedRecords` | 11 | Tombstones carried so the importer can propagate deletions. | Observed |
| `$spl_EorgType` | 10 | Type id scope: LocalId/GlobalId/TableName per exported type. | CrossVerified |
| `$spl_EorgCenter` | 7 | Centre (deployment) id scope. | CrossVerified |
| `$IdEmbeddingFields` | 4 | Per-column ID remap instructions: pk / fk / idpattern. | CrossVerified |
| `$Data_TypeDefDbNames` | 2 | TypeDef id -> physical table name. | Verified |
| `$Data_FieldDefDbNames` | 3 | FieldDef id -> physical column name. | Verified |
| `$basicInfoRelation` | 6 | Relation rows in the shared-infrastructure scope. | Verified |

## Paging

`$Header.PageCount` and `ExportFileNameHelper.GetPages(string, DataRow)` /
`GetPageCount(DataRow)` together show that one logical export can span several
files. Both supplied samples have `PageCount = 1`, so multi-page layout is
**Observed** from the binary and **not** demonstrated by a sample.
